'''James Orvis Berger''' (born April 6, 1950, in [[Minneapolis, Minnesota]])<ref name=statsci/> is an American [[statistician]] best known for his work on [[Bayesian statistics]] and [[decision theory]]. He won the [[COPSS Presidents' Award]], one of the two highest awards in statistics, in 1985 at the age of 35. He received a Ph.D. in mathematics from [[Cornell University]] in 1974. He was a faculty member in the Department of Statistics at [[Purdue University]] until 1997, at which time he moved to the Institute of Statistics and Decision Sciences (now the Department of Statistical Science) at [[Duke University]], where he is currently the Arts and Sciences Professor of Statistics. He was also director of the [[Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute]] from 2002 to 2010, and has been a visiting professor at the University of Chicago since 2011.<ref name=statsci>{{cite journal | doi = 10.1214/088342304000000053 | title = A Conversation with James O. Berger | year = 2004 | author = Wolpert, Robert L. | journal = Statistical Science | volume = 19 | issue = 1 | pages = 205–218| doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | title = ISI Highly Cited: James O. Berger| url = http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?id=2831&cb=6505 | publisher = ISI Web of Knowledge | year = 2003 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Statistical and Applied Mathematical Sciences Institute |url=http://www.samsi.info/index.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080930085408/http://www.samsi.info/index.shtml |archive-date=2008-09-30 }}</ref>
In 2024–25, Berger has been elected as a Hagler Fellow at the [[Hagler Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref name="HaglerBerger">{{cite web
 |title=Dr. James O. Berger – Class of 2024–25
 |url=https://hias.tamu.edu/fellow/dr-james-o-berger/
 |website=Hagler Institute for Advanced Study
 |publisher=Texas A&M University
 |access-date=16 August 2025
}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
 |title=Texas A&M University elects James O. Berger as Hagler Fellow
 |url=https://imstat.org/2024/12/15/texas-am-university-elects-james-o-berger-as-hagler-fellow/
 |website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics
 |date=15 December 2024
 |access-date=16 August 2025
}}</ref> 

== Contributions to science ==
Berger has worked on the decision theoretic bases of [[Bayesian inference]], including advances on the [[Charles Stein (statistician)|Stein]] phenomenon<ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1214/aos/1176345691| title = Selecting a Minimax Estimator of a Multivariate Normal Mean| journal = The Annals of Statistics| volume = 10| pages = 81–92| year = 1982| last1 = Berger | first1 = J. O. | doi-access = free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | doi = 10.1214/aos/1176345009| title = Examples of Berger's Phenomenon in the Estimation of Independent Normal Means| journal = The Annals of Statistics| volume = 8| issue = 3| pages = 572–585| year = 1980| last1 = Brown | first1 = L.| url = https://repository.upenn.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1343&context=statistics_papers| doi-access = free}}</ref> during and after his thesis. He has also greatly contributed to advances in the so-called [[Prior_probability#Uninformative_priors|objective Bayes]] approach where [[prior probability|prior distributions]] are constructed from the structure of the [[Sampling (statistics)|sampling distributions]] and/or of [[Frequentist inference|frequentist properties]]. He is also recognized for his analysis of the opposition between Bayesian and frequentist visions on [[Statistical hypothesis testing|testing statistical hypotheses]], with criticisms of the use of [[p-values]]<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Sellke | first1 = Thomas | last2 = Bayarri | first2 = M. J. | author2-link = M. J. Bayarri | last3 = Berger | first3 = James O. | title = Calibration of p Values for Testing Precise Null Hypotheses | doi = 10.1198/000313001300339950 | journal = [[The American Statistician ]]| volume = 55 | issue = 1 | pages = 62–71 | year = 2001 | jstor = 2685531| s2cid = 396772 }}</ref> and critical levels.

== Awards and honors ==
Berger has received numerous awards for his work: [[Guggenheim Fellowship]], the [[COPSS Presidents' Award]] and the [[R. A. Fisher Lectureship]]. He was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] and to the [[United States National Academy of Sciences|National Academy of Sciences]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite journal | title = Statistician James O. Berger Elected to National Academy of Sciences | url = http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-23153247_ITM | year = 2003 | publisher = PR Newswire }}</ref> In 2004, he was awarded an honorary Doctor of Science degree by [[Purdue University]].<ref>{{Cite journal | title = James O. Berger: Doctor of Science | url = https://www.purdue.edu/uns/html3month/2004/04hondocs/04.Berger.html | publisher = [[Purdue University]] | year = 2004 }}</ref>
